tagline: Connecting the world through innovative satellite and wireless technologies
hero_kpi_rationale: Viasat positions itself as a provider of diversified multi-orbit communications solutions (GEO, MEO, LEO), combining government services, aviation, and enterprise connectivity. The business model relies on vertical integration and optimization of the product and service portfolio.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Portion of revenue that remains after deducting direct production costs.
kpis.description: Gross margin is slightly improving, supported by better operational efficiency and service mix optimization.
kpis.signal: Gross margin slightly improving despite cost pressures.

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: Profit generated before taxes, interest, and other non-operating expenses.
kpis.description: Operating margin is negative due to expenses related to the development and launch of new satellites, particularly in LEO/MEO, and post-acquisition integration costs.
kpis.signal: Negative operating margin due to heavy investments in satellites.

kpis.name: R&D Investment (% of revenue)
kpis.explanation: Portion of revenue reinvested in research and development of new technologies.
kpis.description: Viasat maintains a high level of R&D investment to develop its secure, multi-orbit solutions, particularly in cybersecurity and tactical gateways.
kpis.signal: High R&D rate, typical of innovative technology players.

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures (satellites and infrastructure)
kpis.explanation: Spending to build or enhance physical assets such as satellites or infrastructure.
kpis.description: Capex is driven by the development of new multi-orbit satellite capabilities and the integration of acquired assets.
kpis.signal: High capex related to the deployment of the low Earth orbit (LEO) constellation.

kpis.name: Headcount (employees)
kpis.explanation: Total number of people employed by the company.
kpis.description: Headcount is increasing moderately, primarily in R&D, cybersecurity, and satellite operations management following integration.
kpis.signal: Slight headcount increase, aligned with technical development needs.

kpis.name: Service / Recurring Revenue
kpis.explanation: Regular revenue from service or subscription contracts.
kpis.description: Recurring revenue is growing, driven by IFC services (in-flight connectivity), long-term government contracts, and managed maritime services.
kpis.signal: Growth in recurring revenue, indicating customer retention.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.description: Revenue extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last 7 reported fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Revenue of $4.52 B in the latest fiscal year (FY2025).

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.description: Net income extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last 5 reported fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Net income of -$0.575 B in the latest fiscal year (FY2025).

kpis.name: AI Cloud Mix
kpis.explanation: Percentage of new contracts incorporating artificial intelligence features.
kpis.description: Viasat is beginning to integrate AI into its cybersecurity, satellite traffic management, and tactical gateway offerings, particularly through recent acquisitions.
kpis.signal: AI gradually being integrated into cybersecurity and network management solutions.

kpis.name: Net Bookings
kpis.explanation: Total value of new contracts signed during the year.
kpis.description: Bookings are increasing, particularly in IFC services, secure defense solutions, and government multi-orbit offerings.
kpis.signal: Growth in bookings within government and aviation services.

risks.title: Dependence on government contracts
risks.score_rationale: Viasat is highly dependent on contracts with the U.S. government, which represent a significant portion of revenue. Any changes in budget allocations, defense priorities, or the loss of key contracts could have a material impact on financial results and future growth.

risks.title: Satellite and operational anomaly risks
risks.score_rationale: Viasat faces significant risks related to the construction, launch, and operation of multi-orbit satellites (GEO, MEO, LEO), including launch failures, in-orbit anomalies, capacity losses, and delays in commercial service entry that affect revenue ramp-up.

risks.title: Increased competition in satellite communications
risks.score_rationale: The satellite communications market faces growing competition from new entrants and emerging technologies. Intensifying competition could affect market share, margins, and the ability to maintain competitive positions.

risks.title: Reliance on global supply chain and disruption risks
risks.score_rationale: Viasat depends on a complex global supply chain including contract manufacturers and sole or limited-source suppliers. Bottlenecks, shortages, tariffs, and geopolitical events could impact delivery timelines and costs.

risks.title: Regulatory and spectrum risks
risks.score_rationale: Viasat is subject to strict regulations regarding satellite communications, spectrum use, and government certifications. Regulatory changes or certification delays could impact operations and revenue.

risks.title: Technology dependence and cybersecurity risks
risks.score_rationale: Viasat is highly dependent on satellite technologies and digital systems, exposing the company to risks of cyberattacks, technological obsolescence, and critical technical failures.

risks.title: Acquisition and integration risks
risks.score_rationale: Viasat has undertaken major acquisitions (notably Inmarsat), resulting in integration costs, risks of unrealized synergies, and challenges in aligning cultures and systems.

risks.title: High leverage and financing constraints
risks.score_rationale: Viasat has high debt levels resulting from acquisitions and capex investments. Elevated leverage limits financial flexibility and increases exposure to interest rate fluctuations.

ai_positioning.summary: Although the 10-K does not explicitly mention AI or machine learning in the provided excerpts, Viasat is gradually integrating intelligent capabilities into its cybersecurity, traffic management, and tactical gateway solutions. The positioning remains under development but is oriented toward network security and control applications.
